Tata Trusts argues the resolution is in violation of Articles 104B and 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association. items.title: Saket court acquits former My FM CEO of sexual harassment charges
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Harish M Bhatia, former CEO of My FM, the radio arm of the Dainik Bhaskar Group, of the charges of outraging and insulting the modesty of a woman. Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivangi Vyas of Saket courts held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Court reiterated that a conviction in a sexual offence can be based solely n a complainant's testimony only if the same is of sterling quality. "The conviction in a sexual offence case can be based solely on the testimony of prosecutrix provided her testimony is of sterling quality that is wholly reliable, consistent and inspires confidence," it said. Where the case rests primarily on that testimony, the Court must scrutinize it with greater care to ensure that it is free from material contradictions, improvements, omissions or inherent improbabilities, the judge added. Since the same was not satisfied in the present case, Bhatia was acquitted of all charges. The complainant, then National Programming Head, alleged harassment between 2008 and 2010 at the workplace, office parties and tours. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a Bengaluru-based man accused of helping two Bangladeshi nationals obtain Aadhaar cards by allowing them to stay in his premises. However, the Court refused to quash the case against a government doctor accused of attesting residential proof documents for 14 Bangladeshi nationals to help them obtain Aadhaar cards and other documents. In the order passed on November 18, Justice H P Sandesh held that there was no prima facie material to establish that the property owner had helped the Bangladeshi nationals obtain Aadhaar cards. “When such being the case, when there is no any prima facie material collected by the Investigating Officer during the course of investigation that this petitioner/accused No.24 had helped accused Nos.3 and 4 in getting the Aadhaar card, there cannot be any criminal prosecution against accused No.24,” the Court said. Justice HP Sandesh While denying the relief to the doctor, the Court noted that forensic examination of material sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) confirmed that the signatures belonged to him.
